name.text: Using the sine rule to find a side

questiontext.text:
Consider triangle \(ABC\), where:

  • \(A={@A@}^\circ\)
  • \(B={@B@}^\circ\)
  • \(a=BC={@side_a@}\text{ cm}\)

(a) Calculate the length of side \(b=AC\) using the Sine Rule.

[[input:ans1]]

[[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

Instructions: Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

We are given:

  • \(A={@A@}^\circ\)
  • \(B={@B@}^\circ\)
  • \(a={@side_a@}\text{ cm}\)

We need to calculate the length of side \(b\).

Step 1: Recall the Sine Rule.

The Sine Rule states that:

\(\dfrac{a}{\sin A}=\dfrac{b}{\sin B}\)

Step 2: Rearrange the formula.

Making \(b\) the subject gives:

\(b=\dfrac{a\sin B}{\sin A}\)

Step 3: Substitute the known values.

\(b=\dfrac{{@side_a@}\times\sin{@B@}^\circ}{\sin{@A@}^\circ}\)

Step 4: Calculate the answer.

\(b\approx{@ta1@}\text{ cm}\)

Final Answer:

\(\boxed{b={@ta1@}\text{ cm}}\)

Remember to use degree mode when evaluating the trigonometric ratios and round your answer to 2 decimal places.
